judgment.rationale: Both Skills are the identical Group Guided Reading bullet 'Reads with increasing fluency and expression' under Reading and Phonics, sharing one Learning Component (tags: reading, guided reading, fluency, expression). The first sits at Grade 1 Term 4 (canonical rank 1) and the second at Grade 2 Term 3 (rank 2), so the permitted developmental direction is lower-to-higher grade. The recurrence is not merely generic: the supplied source context shows the Grade 1 Term 4 guided-reading table is paired with phonics work that only 'introduce[s] new consonant blends', while the Grade 2 Term 3 table expects learners to 'use consonant blends and digraphs to build up and break down words', so the same fluency-and-expression goal is applied to decodably harder, more advanced guided-reading texts a year later. Grade 1 fluent, expressive reading of simpler texts plausibly supports success with the Grade 2 expectation. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence and LC metadata are truncated (24 omitted source-evidence items each), so the exact Grade 2 text-complexity wording is not fully visible, and both endpoints and their ancestors carry upstream merge/audit context (Grade and Term banner nodes are merged representatives); confidence is moderated accordingly.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Grade 2 (rank 2) Skill statements under the WRITING skill area and the Handwriting sub-strand: the first in Term 3 ('Copies and writes short words in joined script or cursive writing: 2 and 3 letter words such as an; am; at; it; in; on; of; he; we; us; be; so; see; can; our', identity scope grade=grade 2|term=term 3|skill area=writing|sub strand=handwriting) and the second in Term 4 ('Copies and writes short words in joined script or cursive writing', identity scope grade=grade 2|term=term 4|...). They describe the same joined-script/cursive copying-and-writing capability, and their Learning Components are effectively identical in skill content (tag overlap jaccard 1.0; 'Copies short words...' / 'Writes short words...' on both sides). The only difference is that the Term 4 printed bullet omits the Term 3 exemplar word list; no larger letter set, longer words, longer texts, or greater independence is stated, so there is no pair-specific evidence of expanded capability, and treating the missing 'such as' list as broadened scope would infer content from omitted text while both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each). A permitted Term 3 to Term 4 buildsTowards is therefore not supported. This is nonetheless more than generic repetition: it is the same Handwriting sub-strand skill continuing across consecutive terms of one grade, where Term 3's prescribed 2- and 3-letter starter set and Term 4's general short-word practice are substantively coherent, mutually reinforcing handwriting work. Symmetric relatesTo with null direction and unchanged canonical endpoint order is the correct complete judgment. Upstream audit/merge context on both endpoints and all ancestors (Handwriting sub-strands, WRITING skill areas, merged TERM 3 / TERM 4 banners, merged GRADE 2 banner) and the truncation warnings are retained and materially limit confidence.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade 2 (rank 2), Term 2, Skill Area 'Reading and Phonics', under different printed sub-strands ('Daily Phonic Activities of 15 minutes'/Phonics vs 'Shared Reading'), and are extracted from the same table row (row=3, page 91). 'Reads words from phonics lessons in sentences and other texts' is applied decoding in connected text; 'Identifies key details in what was read such as main characters and setting' is comprehension within teacher-mediated shared reading. These are substantively coherent, complementary components of the same term's reading programme — decoding and meaning-making applied to texts — which is meaningful instructional coherence beyond shared wording (only 'and'/'in' and the broad 'reading' LC tag overlap). However, the evidence shows no substantive extension, increased complexity, greater independence, or dependency: they are concurrent same-term expectations in parallel sub-strands, and shared-reading comprehension at this point is teacher-supported rather than conditioned on independent decoding proficiency. Same-rank, same-term development is therefore not substantiated, so the symmetric relatesTo is the correct complete judgment. Evidence limitations: 24 omitted source evidence items per endpoint and truncated LC evidence for the first endpoint; both endpoints and all listed ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade R (rank 0) Emergent Reading / Phonological-Phonemic Awareness Skills, so direction must follow Term order within the grade. The second SFI sits under TERM 1 ('Identifies whether two given sounds are the same or different: /p/, /p/ [same]; /p/, /d/ [different]') and involves basic auditory discrimination of two isolated phonemes presented in contrast. The first SFI sits under TERM 2 ('Distinguishes aurally between different sounds especially at the beginning of words'), applying that same discrimination capability to sounds embedded in words at word-initial position; the Term 1 row context further shows the earlier analogue limited to 'the beginning of own name', so Term 2 broadens to words generally. Discriminating same/different isolated sounds plausibly supports success in isolating and distinguishing initial sounds within words, so this is pair-specific extension rather than generic repeated wording (shared tokens are only 'different', 'sounds', 'the'). Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and ancestors carry merge/audit context, so judgment rests on the shown statement text, Term/Skill Area placement and LC tags.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit under Shared, Group and Independent Writing (Term 3) in the WRITING skill area, the second at Grade 2 (rank 2) and the first at Grade 3 (rank 3), so a Grade 2 to Grade 3 developmental direction would be permitted. However, the substantive content differs in kind rather than in depth: the Grade 2 statement is connected prose composition (1-2 paragraphs, at least eight sentences, on personal experiences or events), while the Grade 3 statement is summarising and recording information in non-prose graphic formats (mind maps, tables, notices, diagrams, charts). The Grade 3 LCs ('records information...' / 'summarises information...') show no expansion of paragraph writing (no increase in length, sentence count, topic range, or independence relative to the Grade 2 statement); the only overlap flagged by nomination is the generic 'writing' tag, the token 'or', and trigram noise. That supports meaningful coherence as complementary written-recording/composition skills within the same sub-strand, but not a justified claim that paragraph composition supports success in summarising into graphic organisers. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), so absence of further linking detail is not proven; the symmetric reading is nonetheless the best-supported judgment on the bounded evidence.

Coherent reinforcement within the same oral strand supports relatesTo rather than buildsTowards. judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 3 (rank 3) Listening and Speaking (Oral) Skills about working out cause and effect in a story, but they sit in different terms within the grade. The second SFI is Grade 3 Term 2 ('Works out cause and effect in a story using connecting words such as ‘because’'), where the causal link is explicitly cued by a connective. The first SFI is Grade 3 Term 4 ('Listens to a story and works out cause and effect in response to questions such as “What would have happened if the dog had not been found?”'), requiring inferential/counterfactual reasoning about causality in oral response to questioning, without an explicit connective cue. That is substantive deepening rather than mere repeated wording, so proficiency with connective-signalled cause and effect (Term 2) supports success with question-driven causal inference (Term 4); the direction is earlier-to-later term within the same grade, i.e. second_to_first. Endpoint source evidence and some LC metadata are truncated, but the full statement texts and identity scopes (Term 2 vs Term 4) are present and unambiguous.

judgment.rationale: Both are Phonics skills under Reading and Phonics, Term 3, with the same core capability of grouping common words into sound families. The first is Grade 1 (rank 1), where the surrounding Term 3 phonics context is revising single letters and introducing common consonant blends and digraphs; the second is Grade 2 (rank 2), where the same statement is extended to specified vowel-digraph families ('oy'/'oi'; 'ay'/'ai') within a context of using blends and digraphs to build up and break down words. This is substantive extension of the sound-family concept to more complex alternative vowel spellings, so Grade 1 proficiency supports success in Grade 2; lower-to-higher rank direction is first_to_second. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated and carries upstream merge/audit context, but the retained statement text and identity scopes are consistent and sufficient.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 3 (rank 3) Reading and Phonics Skills but sit in different sub-strands and terms: the first is a Term 1 Paired/Independent Reading bullet on playing reading games (Snap, Memory) and completing crosswords to reinforce reading and vocabulary skills; the second is a Term 4 Group Guided Reading bullet on reading silently and aloud from own book in a teacher-led group at the group's instructional level. The shared evidence is only generic ('reading', 'and' token overlap, shared Grade ancestor, zero rank gap), and the activities differ in mode (game-based vocabulary/word-recognition reinforcement versus sustained connected-text reading with teacher guidance). Although Term 1 to Term 4 would be a permitted forward direction within Grade 3, the evidence shows complementary classroom reading routines rather than a substantive deepening or dependency in which game/crossword practice is shown to enable guided instructional-level reading. Meaningful conceptual coherence within the same Grade 3 reading programme supports a symmetric relatesTo. Source-evidence truncation on both endpoints (24 omitted items each) and truncated LC evidence for the second SFI limit how much further detail can be checked.

Proficiency in ordering events logically therefore supports success in delivering a logically sequenced oral presentation, so the permitted same-grade, same-term direction second_to_first is justified by substantive part-to-whole evidence rather than shared ancestry, page proximity, or the generic shared token 'oral'. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all nodes carry upstream audit/merge context, so the judgment rests on the printed statement text, identity scopes and Learning Components supplied; this limits but does not contradict the inference.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 1 Skills (rank 1) but sit in different strands: the first is Term 3 WRITING / 'Shared, Group and Independent Writing' ('Contributes ideas and words for a class story in Shared Writing sessions'), the second is Term 4 LISTENING AND SPEAKING (ORAL) / 'Twice weekly focussed listening and speaking activities' ('Tells a familiar story which has a beginning, middle and end, varying tone and volume of voice'). They share genuine narrative/story-composition coherence — orally generating story language in a teacher-scaffolded class story complements independently telling a structured familiar story with expressive voice — and the LCs ('Contributes ideas and words for a class story', 'Tells a familiar story which has a beginning, middle and end', 'Varies tone and volume of voice') reinforce each other. However, the only lexical evidence is the weak shared token 'story' (LC-tag Jaccard 0.07, SFI text Jaccard 0.125) and neither statement adds capability to the other: contributing ideas in shared writing is not a demonstrated enabler of structured oral retelling with vocal variation, nor the converse, so no developmental dependency is warranted despite the Term 3 to Term 4 ordering permitting first_to_second. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), which limits deeper verification but does not change the coherent-but-non-dependent reading.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade 1 (rank 1), Term 4, Skill Area WRITING, page 81, but under different printed sub-strands: 'Contributes ideas for and helps to revise a class/group story (Shared Writing)' falls under 'Shared, Group and Independent Writing' (LCs: contributing ideas, revising a class story), while 'Copies and writes a sentence correctly' falls under 'Handwriting' (LCs: copies a sentence correctly, writes a sentence correctly). They are complementary components of early writing — oral/collaborative composition and revision on one side, sentence-level transcription and correct formation on the other — so there is genuine conceptual coherence within the same term's writing programme. However, neither statement's evidence shows that proficiency in one supports success in the other: contributing ideas to a teacher-scribed shared story does not require independent sentence transcription, and copying/writing a sentence does not depend on group composition. Identical Grade and Term rank gives no developmental ordering, and the nomination signals (shared ancestors, same page, token overlap on 'a', 'and', 'writing') are generic. judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade 1 (rank 1) under the WRITING Skill Area, sub-strand 'Shared, Group and Independent Writing': the first is Term 1 'Draws pictures to convey a message. For example, about a personal experience'; the second is Term 4 'Begins to use present and past tense correctly in writing'. Term 1 to Term 4 would be a permitted forward direction, but the evidence shows two substantively different capabilities rather than a deepening of one: LC tags are 'drawing/message/personal experience/writing' versus 'grammar/past/present/tense/writing', with only the generic token 'writing' shared. Proficiency in drawing a picture message is emergent meaning-making and does not specifically support grammatical tense accuracy in written text, so a developmental dependency is not justified; they are coherent complementary composition skills within the same Grade 1 writing sub-strand, supporting relatesTo. Both endpoints carry truncated source evidence (24 omitted items each) and merge/audit context, so judgment rests on the bounded excerpts available.
